name: Fastly CDN
description: Protects against destructive Fastly CLI operations like service, domain, \ backend, and VCL deletion.

destructive_patterns.name: fastly-service-delete
destructive_patterns.description: fastly service delete removes a Fastly service entirely.
destructive_patterns.explanation:
Deleting a Fastly service removes ALL associated domains, backends, VCL, \ dictionaries, ACLs, and logging configurations. All traffic to this service \ will immediately fail. Service IDs cannot be reused after deletion.

\ Safer alternatives: \ - fastly service describe: Review service configuration first \ - Export VCL and configuration for backup \ - Remove domains before deleting to confirm no active traffic

destructive_patterns.name: fastly-domain-delete
destructive_patterns.description: fastly domain delete removes a domain from a service.
destructive_patterns.explanation:
Removing a domain from a Fastly service immediately stops CDN handling \ for that domain. Traffic will either fail or fall back to the origin \ directly, bypassing caching and edge features.

\ Safer alternatives: \ - fastly domain list: Review all domains on the service \ - Update DNS before removing from Fastly \ - Test with a staging domain first

destructive_patterns.name: fastly-backend-delete
destructive_patterns.description: fastly backend delete removes a backend origin server.
destructive_patterns.explanation:
Deleting a backend removes an origin server from the service. If VCL or \ routing rules reference this backend, requests will fail with 503 errors. \ Health checks and shield configuration are also removed.

\ Safer alternatives: \ - fastly backend describe: Review backend configuration \ - Update VCL to stop routing to this backend first \ - Add replacement backend before removing the old one

destructive_patterns.name: fastly-vcl-delete
destructive_patterns.description: fastly vcl delete removes VCL configuration.
destructive_patterns.explanation:
Deleting VCL removes custom edge logic including routing, caching rules, \ header manipulation, and security policies. The service may fall back to \ default behavior or fail if the deleted VCL was the main configuration.

\ Safer alternatives: \ - fastly vcl describe: Download VCL content first \ - Keep VCL in version control \ - Create new version before deleting from old

destructive_patterns.name: fastly-dictionary-delete
destructive_patterns.description: fastly dictionary delete removes an edge dictionary.
destructive_patterns.explanation:
Deleting an edge dictionary removes key-value configuration data used by \ VCL. If VCL references this dictionary for routing, feature flags, or \ blocklists, those lookups will fail causing request errors.

\ Safer alternatives: \ - fastly dictionary-item list: Export dictionary contents \ - Update VCL to remove dictionary references first \ - Create replacement dictionary before deleting

destructive_patterns.name: fastly-dictionary-item-delete
destructive_patterns.description: fastly dictionary-item delete removes dictionary entries.
destructive_patterns.explanation:
Deleting dictionary items removes edge configuration values. VCL lookups \ for deleted keys will return empty strings, potentially affecting routing, \ redirects, or feature flag logic.

\ Safer alternatives: \ - Review which VCL snippets use this dictionary \ - Set values to empty instead of deleting if VCL expects the key \ - Back up dictionary contents before modifications

destructive_patterns.name: fastly-acl-delete
destructive_patterns.description: fastly acl delete removes an access control list.
destructive_patterns.explanation:
Deleting an ACL removes IP allowlist or blocklist configuration. Security \ rules referencing this ACL will no longer match, potentially exposing \ protected resources or breaking geo-restriction logic.

\ Safer alternatives: \ - fastly acl-entry list: Export ACL entries first \ - Update VCL to remove ACL references \ - Create replacement ACL before deleting

destructive_patterns.name: fastly-acl-entry-delete
destructive_patterns.description: fastly acl-entry delete removes ACL entries.
destructive_patterns.explanation:
Removing ACL entries changes IP matching behavior. Removing an IP from a \ blocklist allows that IP to access the service. Removing from an allowlist \ blocks that IP.

\ Safer alternatives: \ - Review the ACL purpose (allow vs block list) \ - Verify the entry change with the security team \ - Document why the entry is being removed

destructive_patterns.name: fastly-logging-delete
destructive_patterns.description: fastly logging delete removes logging endpoints.
destructive_patterns.explanation:
Deleting a logging endpoint stops log delivery to that destination. You \ will lose visibility into edge traffic, errors, and security events. \ Compliance and debugging capabilities are affected.

\ Safer alternatives: \ - Ensure alternative logging is configured \ - Export endpoint configuration for backup \ - Disable endpoint before full deletion

destructive_patterns.name: fastly-version-activate
destructive_patterns.description: fastly service version activate can cause service disruption if misconfigured.
destructive_patterns.explanation:
Activating a service version immediately deploys that configuration to all \ edge nodes. Misconfigured VCL, missing backends, or broken routing rules \ will cause immediate outages affecting all traffic.

\ Safer alternatives: \ - fastly vcl validate: Validate VCL syntax first \ - Use fastly diff to compare with current active version \ - Test in a staging service before production activation

destructive_patterns.name: fastly-compute-delete
destructive_patterns.description: fastly compute delete removes compute package.
destructive_patterns.explanation:
Deleting a Compute@Edge package removes your WASM application from the \ service. All serverless edge compute functionality stops immediately. \ The package must be rebuilt and redeployed to restore functionality.

\ Safer alternatives: \ - Keep package source in version control \ - Deploy replacement package before deleting \ - Use fastly compute describe to review current state
